## Further subclustering
```{r}
hsskin.ST <- UpdateSeuratObject(hsskin.ST)

# --- Subcluster Cluster 1 (Basal/Langerhans) ---
Idents(hsskin.ST) <- 'cell_type_minor'

c1_subset <- subset(hsskin.ST, idents = "Naïve CD4+ T Cells")
c1_subset <- FindNeighbors(c1_subset, dims = 1:10)
c1_subset <- FindClusters(c1_subset, graph.name = "SCT_snn", resolution = 0.2) 
# Markers to look for: CD1A/CD207 (Langerhans), MKI67 (Proliferating), KRT15 (Basal)
c1_markers <- FindAllMarkers(c1_subset, only.pos = TRUE)

write.csv(c1_markers, file = "results/260506/c1_markers.csv", row.names = FALSE)


c5_subset <- subset(hsskin.ST, idents = "Age-associated CD8+ T Cells/NK Cells")
c5_subset <- FindNeighbors(c5_subset, dims = 1:10)
c5_subset <- FindClusters(c5_subset, graph.name = "SCT_snn", resolution = 0.2) 
# Markers to look for: CD1A/CD207 (Langerhans), MKI67 (Proliferating), KRT15 (Basal)
c5_markers <- FindAllMarkers(c5_subset, only.pos = TRUE)

write.csv(c5_markers, file = "results/260506/c5_markers.csv", row.names = FALSE)


# Example Sub-Mapping (Adjust labels based on your marker results)
c1_labels <- c("0" = "Fibroblasts", "1" = "Naïve CD4+ T Cells", "2" = "Naïve CD4+ T Cells")
c5_labels <- c(
  "0" = "M2 Macrophages",                  
  "1" = "Fibroblasts",                      # PDGFRA+ / DCN+ Contamination
  "2" = "CD4+ Naïve T Cells",               # SELL+ / NELL2+ / LTB+
  "3" = "CD8+ Exhausted T Cells",      # MKI67+ / IRF8+ Proliferating/Immune
  "4" = "CD8+ Cytotoxic Age-associated T Cells", # CD8A/B+ / ZNF683+ / GZMA+ / GZMH+
  "5" = "CD8+ T Cells",                     # Resting/Skinned Dermal T Cells
  "6" = "Blood Vessel Cells",               # VWF+ / PLVAP+ Endothelial Contamination
  "7" = "B Cells"                           # IGKC+ / JCHAIN+ / MZB1+ Plasma Cells
)

# Apply sub-labels to the subsets
c1_subset$sub_type <- unname(c1_labels[as.character(Idents(c1_subset))])
c5_subset$sub_type <- unname(c5_labels[as.character(Idents(c5_subset))])
c8_subset$sub_type <- unname(c8_labels[as.character(Idents(c8_subset))])

# Start with your existing minor labels
hsskin.ST$cell_type_final <- as.character(hsskin.ST$cell_type_minor)

# Replace the broad labels with the specific sub-labels using cell IDs
hsskin.ST$cell_type_final[colnames(c1_subset)] <- c1_subset$sub_type
hsskin.ST$cell_type_final[colnames(c5_subset)] <- c5_subset$sub_type
hsskin.ST$cell_type_final[colnames(c8_subset)] <- c8_subset$sub_type

# Final visualization
# Define a high-contrast palette for your specific labels
# High-distinction palette based on your color families
final_colors <- c(
  # =========================================================================
  # 1) Keratinocyte / Epidermal Family (Browns, Tans, Reds)
  # =========================================================================
  "Basal Keratinocytes"                   = "#dfc299", # Golden Tan
  "Spinous Keratinocytes"                 = "#a0816c", # Wood Brown
  "Suprabasal Keratinocytes"              = "#6e5646", # Dark Bark Brown
  "Corneocytes"                           = "#a52829", # Deep Brick Red
  "Hair Follicles"                        = "#d14949", # Coral Red
  
  # =========================================================================
  # 2) Stromal / Structural Family (Greens & Blues)
  # =========================================================================
  "Fibroblasts"                           = "#136432", # Forest Green
  "Blood Vessel Cells"                    = "#4393c3", # Steel Blue
  "Smooth Muscle Cells"                   = "#6a3d9a", # Deep structural Violet
  
  # =========================================================================
  # 3) Lymphoid Immune Compartment (High-Contrast Pinks, Magentas, Plums)
  # =========================================================================
  "CD4+ Naïve T Cells"                    = "#ff69b4", # Bright Hot Pink
  "CD8+ T Cells"                          = "#c51b7d", # Classic Deep Pink
  "CD8+ Exhausted T Cells"                = "#de77ae", # Soft Pastel Pink
  "CD8+ Cytotoxic Age-associated T Cells"  = "#4d004b", # Blackberry (Very dark black-purple)
  "B Cells"                               = "#984ea3", # Vibrant Orchid Purple
  
  # =========================================================================
  # 4) Myeloid Immune Compartment (Moved out of Pink into Teal, Orange, Gold)
  # =========================================================================
  "Dendritic Cells"                       = "#ffd700", # Bright Gold
  "Langerhans Cells"                      = "#fcae91", # Warm Light Apricot / Peach
  "Macrophages"                           = "#01665e", # Deep Dermal Teal
```

```{r}
library(Seurat)
library(dplyr)
library(writexl) # installation: install.packages("writexl")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Extract and Clean FOV Coordinates (Your Pipeline Logic)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
fov_names <- Images(hsskin.ST)

extract_fov_coords <- function(obj, fov_name) {
  coords <- GetTissueCoordinates(obj[[fov_name]])
  coords <- as.data.frame(coords)
  coords$cell_id <- rownames(coords)
  coords$fov <- fov_name
  
  # Find numeric columns dynamically (x and y)
  numeric_cols <- names(coords)[sapply(coords, is.numeric)]
  if (length(numeric_cols) < 2) {
    stop(paste("Could not find at least two numeric coordinate columns for", fov_name))
  }
  
  coords <- coords %>%
    rename(
      x = all_of(numeric_cols[1]),
      y = all_of(numeric_cols[2])
    )
  
  return(coords)
}

# Combine coordinates across all FOVs
coords_all <- bind_rows(lapply(fov_names, function(f) extract_fov_coords(hsskin.ST, f)))

# Clean or align cell naming conventions
if ("cell" %in% colnames(coords_all)) {
  coords_all <- coords_all %>%
    select(-cell_id) %>%
    rename(cell_id = cell)
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2) Extract and Select Requested Metadata Columns
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
metadata_df <- hsskin.ST@meta.data

# Build structured data frame incorporating age and sample
md_clean <- data.frame(
  cell_id         = rownames(metadata_df),
  age             = if("age" %in% colnames(metadata_df)) metadata_df$age else NA,
  sample          = if("sample" %in% colnames(metadata_df)) metadata_df$sample else NA,
  cell_type_major = if("cell_type_major" %in% colnames(metadata_df)) metadata_df$cell_type_major else NA,
  cell_type_minor = if("cell_type_minor" %in% colnames(metadata_df)) metadata_df$cell_type_minor else NA,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Dynamically pull the correct senescence definition column (snc or snc2)
if ("snc" %in% colnames(metadata_df)) {
  md_clean$snc <- metadata_df$snc
} else if ("snc2" %in% colnames(metadata_df)) {
  md_clean$snc <- metadata_df$snc2
} else {
  md_clean$snc <- NA
  warning("Neither 'snc' nor 'snc2' column was found in the metadata.")
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3) Merge, Order Columns, and Save Workbook
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
excel_data <- coords_all %>%
  left_join(md_clean, by = "cell_id") %>%
  select(cell_id, x, y, fov, age, sample, cell_type_major, cell_type_minor, snc)

# Save Workbook
output_excel_path <- "results/260523/xenium_skin_comprehensive_metadata.xlsx"
write_xlsx(excel_data, path = output_excel_path)

cat("Successfully compiled spatial coordinates, demographics, and annotations into Excel:\n", 
    getwd(), "/", output_excel_path, "\n", sep="")
```




```{r}
library(Seurat)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Subset Object to Keep "Old" Cohort and Filter NAs
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
obj_old_pos <- subset(
  x = hsskin.ST,
  subset = age == "Old" & 
           !is.na(cell_type_minor) & 
           !is.na(snc)  # Adjust to "snc2" if that is your active flag column
)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2) Restrict Order Array STRICTLY to Skin Structural Populations
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Structural vertical tissue layer hierarchy omitting immune subsets
custom_axis_order <- c(
  "Muscle Cells",
  "Endothelial Cells",
  "Melanocytes",
  "Dermal Fibroblasts",
  "Reticular Fibroblasts",
  "Papillary Fibroblasts",
  "Hair Follicle Cells",
  "Bulge Keratinocytes",
  "Basal Keratinocytes",
  "Spinous Keratinocytes",
  "Granular Keratinocytes"
)

# Keep only cells matching your structural list
cells_to_keep <- rownames(obj_old_pos@meta.data)[obj_old_pos$cell_type_minor %in% custom_axis_order]
obj_old_pos <- subset(obj_old_pos, cells = cells_to_keep)

# Lock in the anatomical sequence
obj_old_pos$cell_type_minor <- factor(
  obj_old_pos$cell_type_minor, 
  levels = custom_axis_order
)

# Assign identities for the DotPlot engine
Idents(obj_old_pos) <- "cell_type_minor"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3) Generate the Base Multi-Feature Matrix Plot 
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
p_base <- DotPlot(
  object = obj_old_pos,
  features = c("CDKN2A", "CDKN1A"), # Human gene symbols
  assay = "Xenium",                 
  col.min = NULL, 
  col.max = NULL  
) + 
  scale_color_gradientn(
    colors = c("#2166ac", "#67a9cf", "#f7f7f7", "#ef8a62", "#b2182b"),
    #name = "CDKN2A (p16)\nMean Expression"
  )

# Save high-resolution vectorized output layout
ggsave(
  filename = "results/260523/xenium_skin_structural_unscaled_dotplot.pdf",
  plot = p_base,
  width = 6.2, 
  height = 5.5,
  dpi = 300
)
```
